slides.title: Before the Toyota War
slides.body:
The final phase of the Chadian-Libyan conflict began when unified Chadian forces challenged Libya's fortified occupation of northern Chad.

The Conflict Takes Shape: The campaign would decide control of northern Chad and expose whether Libya's larger, heavily equipped army could hold the desert. The opening phase established the political goals, alliances, and military problems that shaped every later campaign.

slides.cap: Opening context for the Toyota War

slides.title: Ouadi Doum air raid
slides.body:
The Ouadi Doum airstrike was carried out by the French Air Force on 16 February 1986, against the Libyan airbase of Ouadi Doum in northern Chad, during the Chadian–Libyan conflict. The raid was significant in that it demonstrated French resolve to counter Gaddafi's expansionary aims and indicated France's commitment to its former colonies.

Why This Moment Matters: Ouadi Doum air raid was more than an isolated engagement. It helped define the conflict's direction and exposed the strengths and weaknesses of the opposing sides. The campaign would decide control of northern Chad and expose whether Libya's larger, heavily equipped army could hold the desert.

Consequences: The effects of Ouadi Doum air raid extended beyond its immediate result. The rapid campaign reduced prolonged occupation but brought intense fighting and losses around bases and desert communities. Its place in the wider campaign also influenced later military choices and political calculations.

slides.title: Battle of Fada
slides.body:
The Battle of Fada took place in northern Chad in 1987, and was a turning point of the Chadian–Libyan conflict.

slides.title: Battle of Aouzou
slides.body:
The Battle of Aouzou refers to a pair of battles fought between Chad and Libya in and around the town of Aouzou (Chad) in August 1987, as part of the Toyota War, the last phase of the larger Chadian–Libyan conflict. The first battle resulted in a Chadian victory, while the second battle, a Libyan counteroffensive, is deemed to have been won by Libya.

Why This Moment Matters: Battle of Aouzou was more than an isolated engagement. It reflected the changing balance of power and pushed the conflict closer to its eventual outcome. The campaign would decide control of northern Chad and expose whether Libya's larger, heavily equipped army could hold the desert.

Consequences: The effects of Battle of Aouzou extended beyond its immediate result. The rapid campaign reduced prolonged occupation but brought intense fighting and losses around bases and desert communities. Its place in the wider campaign also influenced later military choices and political calculations.

slides.title: Battle of Maaten al-Sarra
slides.body:
The Battle of Maaten al-Sarra was fought between Chad and Libya on September 5, 1987, during the Toyota War. The battle took the form of a surprise Chadian raid against the Libyan Maaten al-Sarra Air Base, meant to remove the threat of Libyan airpower, that had already thwarted the Chadian attack on the Aouzou Strip in August. The first clash ever held in Libyan territory since the beginning of the Chadian–Libyan conflict, the attack was fully successful, causing a high number of Libyan casualties and low Chadian casualties, also contributing to the definitive ceasefire signed on September 11 among the warring countries.

Why This Moment Matters: Battle of Maaten al-Sarra was more than an isolated engagement. It reflected the changing balance of power and pushed the conflict closer to its eventual outcome. The campaign would decide control of northern Chad and expose whether Libya's larger, heavily equipped army could hold the desert.

sub: How the Toyota War ended and what followed

slides.title: The End of the Toyota War
slides.body: Chadian units using fast civilian trucks outmaneuvered and destroyed Libyan formations, forcing Libya to accept a ceasefire.
